summary.intent: Work through the NEXT-WORK plan for the callisto release tool (cleanup, test debt, SYS-RETRY, SYS-NAPI, refactors), then perf and hardening: batched git reads, tag-annotation hints, michi 0.6 adoption, and look patience in the release wave.
summary.outcome: Opened and shipped many PRs (#202-#208, perf stack, #336-#338 merged, #339 hints reader, #341 look patience). After measurement showed the hints saved about one git process within noise, the user rejected them as over-engineering, and the assistant began reverting the hints writer and closing #339 and #335.

repo: Plans and handoff docs for local tracking live in .claude/plans/ and are excluded via .git/info/exclude; they must never be committed or put in a PR.
Run `just ci` per worktree, one at a time. A background-task 'exit code 0' notification only reports the wrapper script; read the log's own `VERDICT exit=` line.

Squash-merged stacked PRs leave the remote branch with pre-squash commits. Merge main into the branch or use `git rebase --onto`, and avoid force-pushing. Use `gh stack unstack` then `gh stack link` when a stack has a closed PR.

Clippy in this repo disallows placeholder binding names like `foo`, and a stray `crates/.claude` directory (created when cwd is inside crates/) breaks cargo metadata and insta. Always run from the repo root.
Release harness fakes (gh, cargo, registry) can hide bugs. The plan requires proving fixes with the real tool, and specs in docs/specs/*.json need criteria updated alongside behavior changes.
The sealed release intent does not include tag annotation text, so annotation changes never alter intent digests (the original ADR 13 claim was wrong).
The performance gains since v0.12 come from batching: git process count went from thousands to 6-11 per command, giving 50-115x speedups on synthetic fixtures.
The single ruleset 'main branch' covers only refs/heads/main (signed commits, PR, merge queue) and not tags. Release workflow `execute` has contents: write and pushes annotated tags.
Tag hints add about 128 bytes per tag and save roughly one git process, which was indistinguishable from noise.

code.finding: Each confirmation look now gets the remaining wave window as its patience, recomputed per look. A fixed patience let three looks in one pass each spend the full window (1080s vs 360s).

Local release selection now observes releases already tagged at HEAD across registry, tag and GitHub release, so a rerun after a failed tag push finishes the release (SYS-RETRY). A tag on an older commit still settles without contacting providers.
The napi roster is derived per intent package via `callisto matrix`, and the placement step reads the plan job's napi_dirs output. macOS bash lacks `mapfile`, so a portable read loop is needed.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, and mutation-test new characterization tests (revert or alter source to confirm they fail) when they pass on the first run.
Commit snapshot/characterization tests before mechanical moves so the snapshots prove the move is behavior-preserving.
Measure on a loaded machine with interleaved runs and process counts, not wall-clock percentages; count git processes for a noise-free metric.
Do not add code paths (e.g. hint reading) whose measured benefit is within noise. Ask whether the value is meaningful before building cleverness.
Check local checkouts (e.g. ~/projects/michi) before fetching upstream sources through scratch crates.
The sandbox rejects heredocs, compound commands and inline scripts mentioning git, so write script files and run them separately.

friction: Misplaced the NEXT-WORK plan in a PR (#201), which the user had to point out; it was closed and moved to a local excluded file.
Sandbox guard rejected heredocs, compound commands, git config writes and writes to the jobs dir, forcing script-file workarounds and running CI outside the sandbox.
A first v0.12 comparison script hid its output and hung for hours on a single 10,000-package status run.
Timing measurements were noisy because other processes (rustc, codex, syspolicyd) loaded the machine.
The first ADR 13 draft contained an incorrect sealed-digest claim, and earlier perf claims (5x cheaper batch, 2GB cache) had to be corrected.
The assistant fetched michi sources via a scratch crate when a local checkout existed, and the user rebuked it.
Cannot edit the shared checkout's .claude/plans file from the background worktree session.
The PR body used literal backslash-escaped backticks, which had to be fixed after opening.
